title: Washing finished embroidery
subtitle: How to wash and rinse a finished embroidery without damaging the stitches or cloth.
excerpt: Finished embroidery needs careful washing to remove water-soluble pen marks, handling grime, and hoop marks. The method is straightforward: cold water, no rubbing, a gentle squeeze, rolled in a towel and dried flat. This technique entry covers each step.
sourceNotes: Washing and finishing guidance synthesised from contemporary needlework practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The final wash given to a completed embroidery to remove marker traces, hoop marks, and handling grime. Done in cold water with a small amount of gentle detergent before the piece is blocked and dried flat.

content.text: is the first step in presenting finished embroidery. It removes the visible traces of the working process and prepares the piece for blocking. Always test any thread or fabric for colourfastness before the first full wash.

Test colourfastness on a short thread end. Hold a damp white cloth against the thread and press. If colour transfers, the thread is not fast and the piece should be handled dry or finished without washing. Red and dark blue threads are most likely to bleed.
Fill a clean basin with cool water. Add a very small amount of gentle wool-wash liquid. Do not use biological detergent.
Lower the embroidery into the water and gently move it around. Do not rub or wring.
Let it soak for five minutes.
Lift the piece out and rinse in cool clean water. Repeat the rinse until no suds remain.
Roll the piece gently in a clean dry towel to remove excess water.
Unroll and dry flat, away from direct sunlight. Do not hang wet embroidery; the weight of the water stretches the cloth.

items.symptom: Threads bleed colour onto the fabric
items.fix: Rinse immediately in cold running water. Blot, do not rub. If bleeding has occurred, further washing won't remove it. Next time test all threads before starting.

items.symptom: The water-soluble pen marks are still visible after washing
items.cause: The water was too warm, or the piece was ironed before washing.
items.fix: Soak again in cool water for 20 minutes. If marks persist, the heat from ironing may have set them. Always remove pen marks with cold water before ironing.
